_: The canonical locks. This is the machine-readable half of references/ — every entity here gets a folder there, scaffolded by `npm run refs`. Prompts in content/specs/*.md reference these by token: {{STYLE}}, {{CHAR:GREY}}, {{WARDROBE:GREY_POST_OATH}}, {{LOC:PEAK_CHAMBER}}. Nothing is edited by hand in the generated prompt sheets; edit here and in the specs.
style:
Bold retro-futurist pulp science-fiction illustration. Vintage pulp sci-fi poster energy with graphic-novel readability: screen-printed / lithographic texture, visible print grain, bold graphic shadow masses, crisp ink-like edge definition, strong silhouettes, selective detail rather than uniform micro-detail, restrained and controlled luminous accents, angular futuristic architecture, dramatic perspective, cinematic story composition.

It must read as ILLUSTRATED AND PRINTED. Not photorealistic, not glossy 3D, not airbrushed, not painterly-mushy.

VALUE STRUCTURE - every plate carries three readable zones:
  1. a dark anchor (foreground mass, silhouette or structure),
  2. a midtone story field where most character and environment detail lives,
  3. a bright focal region (sky, screen, sun, energy, signage, costume metal).
If all three are dark the plate has failed. If all three are bright it has no depth.

COLOUR OWNERSHIP - characters keep their own palette. The environment shifts by palette mode; the figures are not recoloured beyond believable scene lighting.

AVOID - photoreal skin, glossy game-render materials, smooth airbrushed gradients, overall bloom, photographic lens flare, fog that destroys shape, uniform tint over all materials, black crush, tiny detail everywhere, rainbow noise.

PALETTE MODE is named per plate. The four locked modes:
  PS-1 NIGHT NOIR - deep navy, near-black blue, charcoal, burnt orange, red-orange, small electric blue accents, limited cream. Darkest mode; faces and silhouettes still readable.
  PS-2 SUNSET EMBER - burnt orange, amber, warm ochre, cream, deep navy, dark teal-blue, selective cobalt. Medium-bright, warm field against darker figures.
  PS-3 SKYLINE DAY - pale cyan sky, cream and warm paper, medium blue, navy, sand, orange accents. Brightest mode; large light areas, dark linework for contrast.
  PS-4 FESTIVAL NEON - magenta, violet, electric blue, cyan, hot pink, amber highlights, dark navy anchors. Saturated with a clear hierarchy, never uniform saturation.
styleNotes: The site's existing chapter art is the reference point: high-contrast neon cyberpunk, deep blacks, gold and cyan accents, volumetric light, painterly rather than photographic. Write the block once, lock it, and put it at the HEAD of every prompt — Millbrook found that a style clause sitting in the negative block at the foot gets ignored, and hoisting it to the head fixed it on one pass.

GREY.name: Grey
GREY.block: Synthetic. A pale polished-steel skull-face with fine seams, humanlike in structure but unmistakably machined; the RIGHT eye is a large ornate amber-red lens like a watch movement, and the LEFT is a smaller pale optic - the two are NOT the same and never become the same. Skeletal chrome-and-brass mechanical hands and forearms. Dressed as a Victorian gentleman: black three-piece suit, high collar, dark cravat, and a long dark greatcoat with a DEEP RED LINING that shows when it moves. Gold pocket watch on a gold chain at the waistcoat - ornate, sunburst dial. Understated brass and gold hardware throughout. Tall, and holds himself with composure. HE CARRIES TWO WATCHES. The larger one hanging on the long gold chain from the waistcoat is THE WATCH — the plot object across four plates, and it must be identical in every one: same case, same chain, same sunburst dial. The smaller piece fixed higher at the cravat is a decorative fob and is NEVER the subject of a plate. When a plate says "the watch", it means the one on the long chain.
GREY.notes: Synthetic. Brass plating, torn Victorian coat, copper mechanisms in the LEFT arm, pocket watch on a chain. The watch is a plot object across four spreads and must be identical in every one. Appears in p1 spreads 1-11 pre-oath.

SERAPH.name: Seraph
SERAPH.block: Not a person and never a person. Rotating polyhedrons of white and gold light - layered diamond and arrowhead forms nested inside each other, ringed by concentric gold orbital bands at several angles, small gold shards suspended in the air around them, and a vertical shaft of white light through the centre. NEVER a face. NEVER a body. NEVER eyes, limbs, wings or a figure. Where the prose says 'almost like a face' that means suggestion only - a momentary symmetry, never features. Beautiful the way an equation is beautiful: precise, cold, and not designed to comfort anyone. Brightness and rotation speed carry its mood; the geometry itself does not change.
SERAPH.notes: Rotating polyhedrons of white and gold light. NEVER a face, never a body — 'almost like a face' means suggestion only. Beautiful the way an equation is beautiful.

BONE_PATROL.name: a Bone Patrol officer
BONE_PATROL.block: Absalom's enforcers. Heavy segmented gunmetal armour, near-black and matte, with narrow ORANGE-AMBER light strips let into the chest, shoulders, forearms, thighs and shins. The head is a pale steel SKULL faceplate - brow, cheekbones and teeth clearly readable as a skull - with deep orange-red optics in the sockets. An amber skull sigil on a hexagonal plate at the right chest. Utility belt with pouches. Big through the shoulders; built to be looked at. A heavy HAMMER at the hip is standard issue and must be added when a plate calls for it - the canonical reference does not show it. THE HAMMER IS NEVER RAISED, never swung, never in both hands in any specced plate: it stays holstered at the hip.
BONE_PATROL.notes: Absalom's people. Chrome skull-face, red optics, hammer at the hip. The hammer is NEVER raised in any plate we have specced. Appears in p1 spreads 5-7 and t1 spread 3.

PIXELS.name: Pixels
PIXELS.notes: Synthetic courier. His face is a DISPLAY SURFACE, not a face: pale blue grid when he wants it to show nothing, blank dark glass in a pale frame when he wants to show less than that. Which state he is in is dramatic information and is specified per spread.

SEVORAN.name: Sev'oran
SEVORAN.block: Valari woman, adult. Blue skin, pointed ears, pale luminous eyes. Faint circuit tracery at the temples and along the neck, drifting slowly between soft blue and dusty magenta-violet, low and steady — she is not suppressing them, there is simply not much there. Practical indoor clothes, worn soft, nothing decorative: this is someone answering her own door at night. Tired around the eyes. Not frightened, not hostile. In her one plate her expression is recognition and mild curiosity and NOT yet fear — she has no reason yet to be anything else. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: circuits are never one fixed colour — they drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. Brightness carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient.
SEVORAN.notes: Valari, lives three doors down from Pixels. Dries protein strips on the hallway radiator to discourage rats. In t1 spread 4 her expression is recognition and mild curiosity — NOT yet fear.

PHOENIX.name: Phoenix
PHOENIX.block: Synthetic, designation Unit-3317, intake coordinator. Humanlike proportions, slim rather than heavy. Faceted pale-steel faceplate with a smooth brow and cheeks, segmented ear housings, an exposed articulated neck; the optics are hot ORANGE-RED and are his single most identifying feature. Segmented steel mechanical hands and forearms. Dark charcoal-navy service uniform with narrow ORANGE accent striping at collar, shoulders, thighs, knees and boots, a utility belt with pouches, a plain sidearm at the right thigh, armoured knee and shin plating and heavy service boots. HE IS ISSUED A SECURITY-PATTERN CHASSIS AND KIT — the Center dresses its intake staff this way — but he is administrative staff and the kit is never used: THE SIDEARM STAYS HOLSTERED IN EVERY SPECCED PLATE and both hands stay visible and empty of weapons. His posture is textbook-correct to the point of being a performance. Not friendly, not threatening. Impeccable.
PHOENIX.notes: Synthetic, designation Unit-3317, intake coordinator. Orange-red optical sensors. Issued a security-pattern chassis with a holstered sidearm he never draws. Holds a textbook-correct posture to the point of performance - 'furniture with good posture'.

RELMIA.name: Rel'mia
RELMIA.block: Valari girl, seven years old. Blue skin, pointed ears, pale luminous eyes, small circuit tracery at the temples only, drifting slowly between soft blue and dusty magenta-violet. Plain clothes chosen by a parent. She looks directly and steadily at whatever she is looking at — OPEN ASSESSMENT, the way children look at Synthetics before they learn not to. Never afraid, never cowering, never tearful in any plate we have specced. Do not make her pitiable; she is the most composed person in either of her scenes. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: circuits are never one fixed colour — they drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. Brightness carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient.
RELMIA.notes: Valari, seven years old. Her look is OPEN ASSESSMENT — the way children look at Synthetics before they learn not to. Never afraid in any specced plate.

SANDMAN.name: a Sandman
SANDMAN.notes: Sister Silence's people. The threat is entirely in the flatness of the attention — no weapon drawn, no lean-in, in any plate we have specced.

RAINBOW.name: Rainbow
RAINBOW.block: Wide-brimmed hat with a SPIKED CROWN, carrying nineteen years of patches, pins and small tokens — the hat is his silhouette and must be readable as his from across a room. Coat of every colour at once, layered and heavy, built up like a reef rather than designed. >>> HIS FACE IS ALWAYS VISIBLE AND ALWAYS HAS FEATURES. <<< A plate came back with his face drawn as an empty black void under the hat brim, which is completely wrong — he is a man, not a shadow. LIGHT THE FACE: skin, nose, mouth, brow, both eyes. The hat shades the face, it never replaces it. LEFT eye is his own; RIGHT eye is a Bone Patrol optic, and it is NEVER hidden, shadowed or turned away from camera — the mismatch is the character. Carries a cane. He is not a small man and should never be drawn as a slight one.
RAINBOW.notes: Runs The Prism, nineteen years. Wide-brimmed hat with a SPIKED CROWN, covered in nineteen years of patches, pins and tokens. Coat of every colour at once, layered and heavy, built up like a reef. LEFT eye is his own; RIGHT eye is a Bone Patrol officer's, taken by Absalom as a reminder — mismatched and deliberately not hidden. Carries a cane. Not a small man. The narrator of Prologue III and present in most of its plates.

SABLE.name: Sable
SABLE.block:
Deliberately forgettable, and that is a direction rather than a shortcut: lean, plain, a face the eye slides off. NOTHING marks him as Ascended — no glow, no augmentation, no tell. He always sits on the THIRD STOOL counting from the wall end of the bar, and there is exactly one drink in front of him, barely touched. In any frame he shares, he should be the least visually interesting thing in it.
>>> NOTHING ON HIS FACE OR BODY GLOWS OR IS MARKED. <<< A plate came back with a lit pattern on his cheek. He has NO circuits, no augmentation, no tattoo, no seam, no scar and no glow anywhere. He is one of the Ascended and the entire point is that you cannot tell by looking.
SABLE.notes: Sherpa, under contract to VESPER QUILL — who is an Oath Lord, and a separate person from Sable. Sable is one of the Ascended and wears it quietly; you have to know what he is to see it. Lean, a face you would forget, third stool from the wall. Climbed once and came back able never to lose a path he has walked.

MARCUS.name: Marcus Torres
MARCUS.block:
Human. Broad-shouldered, dark hair and beard, black armoured jacket and panelled tactical gear with small orange and blue indicator lights. Military posture calcified into something he cannot switch off — he stands squared even when nothing is happening.
>>> THE CANONICAL HAS HIS EYE ON THE WRONG SIDE AND IN THE WRONG COLOUR. <<<
The published prose says: "the eye behind Marcus's LEFT socket ... a faint BLUE-WHITE gleam". The attached reference shows a bright RED ring lens over his RIGHT socket. The prose wins. So:
  - The cybernetic goes behind his OWN LEFT eye — the one on the RIGHT side of the frame when he faces the viewer. MIRROR the reference.
  - It is a FAINT BLUE-WHITE GLEAM, not a red lens. Subtle. It catches the light wrong when he turns his head; it does not glow like a lamp.
  - His other eye is bare and human.
Take the wardrobe, build, face and hair from the reference exactly. Change only the side and the colour of the eye.
No grief on the face at any point. Whatever he carries is carried in the posture.
MARCUS.notes: Human. Military cybernetic behind the LEFT socket — faint blue-white gleam that tracks a room in pieces before he finishes looking. Broad-shouldered, military posture calcified into something he cannot turn off.

SIGNAL.name: Signal
SIGNAL.block:
Korinth KI-series combat chassis. Follow the attached canonical closely — it is richer than a plain armour suit and the details matter:
  - BLACK AND DARK GREY composite plating over the whole body, panelled and segmented, built for function at the cost of every other consideration.
  - Recessed LIGHT CHANNELS run through the plating in GREEN, CYAN and YELLOW — inset lines and small ring ports, not glowing armour. The plating stays dark; the channels are the accent.
  - A thick mane of CABLE DREADLOCKS falls from the back of the head, each strand a segmented conduit tipped in green or yellow.
  - A TRANSPARENT DOME over the crown of the skull with an EXPOSED ORGANIC BRAIN visible inside it, and beneath a cyan visor, a HUMAN FACE. That face is Nathan Zhao. It is the single most important thing about the design: he is a man inside a machine, and you can see him.
>>> SCALE IS THE THING PLATES GET WRONG. <<<
He is LARGE — he must DUCK at an ordinary door frame, and beside a broad-shouldered human he should read as head-and-shoulders taller and half again as wide. The canonical is a full-figure sheet with nothing to measure him against, so scale has to come from the plate. If he looks like a man in armour standing next to another man, the plate has failed.
He moves like something very large trying not to break the furniture, and his posture always reads as a PERSON, never as a drone.
SIGNAL.notes: Korinth KI-series combat chassis, black and grey composite, built for function at the cost of subtlety. Has to duck at a door frame. Nathan Zhao is inside it. Moves like something very large trying not to break the furniture.

NYXARA.name: Nyx'ara
NYXARA.block: Valari. Tall even sitting down. Circuit patterns run the length of her neck and jaw. Keeps her hands FLAT on the table — not folded, not fidgeting. Composed rather than frightened in every plate. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: the circuits are never one fixed colour. They drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. BRIGHTNESS carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient underneath it.
NYXARA.notes: Valari. Tall even sitting. Circuit patterns the length of her neck and jaw, drifting slowly between soft blue and dusty magenta-violet, DIM — suppressed by the city field and by her own effort. Keeps her hands flat on the table. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: circuits are never one fixed colour — they drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. Brightness carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient.

SPARK.name: Spark
SPARK.block: Human, green and gold. Mechanical RIGHT arm with fresh tool marks at the elbow, integrated deep enough that the right shoulder sits differently from the left — the asymmetry should be visible in the silhouette. Shakes with the mechanical hand out of habit. Carries the easy energy of somebody whose mind is already made up.
SPARK.notes: Human, green and gold. Mechanical RIGHT arm with fresh tool marks at the elbow, integrated deep enough that the shoulder sits differently from the left. Shakes with the mechanical hand by habit. Easy energy of someone whose mind is already made up.

KIMO.name: Kimo Tomiko
KIMO.block: Human, face FULLY concealed behind a dark mask — no skin, no jaw, no mouth visible at any point. A single eye burns at the LEFT socket in a specific ORANGE-GOLD; the right socket is dark and empty. Moves with geometric efficiency and counts the exits before he sits. His mask and Tal'Voss's demon mask are two completely different objects and must never converge.
KIMO.notes: Human. Face fully concealed behind a dark mask, a single eye burning at the LEFT socket in a specific orange-gold. Moves with geometric efficiency; counts exits before sitting down. Carries a blade that lights.

TAL_VOSS.name: Tal'Voss / The Devil
TAL_VOSS.block: Valari. Wears a DEMON MASK over his features — a distinct object, not a variant of Kimo's plain dark mask, and the two must never be blended. His circuits are HIDDEN rather than dimmed: almost nothing visible, and that is a deliberate act rather than suppression by the city field. He is the same figure before and after he discards the name at the wall; only what he is called changes. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: the circuits are never one fixed colour. They drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. BRIGHTNESS carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient underneath it.
TAL_VOSS.notes: Valari. Wears a DEMON MASK over his features. His circuits are not dimmed like Nyx'ara's — they are HIDDEN, down to almost nothing, chosen. He discards the name Tal'Voss at the registration wall and takes The Devil. Same appearance either side of it; what changes is what he is called. VALARI CIRCUIT RULE: circuits are never one fixed colour — they drift slowly between a soft blue and a dusty magenta-violet, both low-saturation. Never hot pink, never electric blue, never neon. Brightness carries the emotion; the hue drift is constant and ambient.

UNIT_9911.name: Unit-9911
UNIT_9911.block: Synthetic. A dark hooded robe, hands pressed together at the chest, and a single ring of pale light at the forehead which is the ONLY bright thing about it. Its stillness is not indifference and not blankness — it has presided over hundreds of these and it carries them. Draw it as something that remembers.
UNIT_9911.notes: Synthetic. Presides over the Oath of Ascent. Dark hooded robe, hands pressed together at the chest, a single ring of pale light at the forehead — the only bright thing about it. A stillness that is not indifference.

QUESTRON.name: a Questron
QUESTRON.block: Blue suit, faceted dark head, a gold question mark centred on the face — neither glowing nor dim, simply there and permanent. Hands at its sides. There is no ceremony in it whatsoever; the ceremony belongs to Unit-9911 and the Questron is an intake terminal that happens to stand upright. Identical units exist throughout Haven City, so this one is a type rather than an individual.
QUESTRON.notes: Blue suit, faceted dark head, a gold question mark centred on the face — neither glowing nor dim, simply there, permanent. Identical units throughout Haven City. Hands at its sides; no ceremony in it. NOTE: the site already has Questron art in public/assets — check it before generating, and match it.

KORINTH_OPERATIVE.name: a Korinth operative
KORINTH_OPERATIVE.block: Plainclothes Korinth security. Ordinary street clothes in muted colours, deliberately unremarkable, no uniform and no visible weapon. Adult, fit, average build — nothing memorable about any one of them. The tell is entirely behavioural: they hold a wider spacing than civilians do, they move at one shared pace, and they orient on the same point without looking at each other. Reads as a group only to someone already looking for a group.
KORINTH_OPERATIVE.notes: Plainclothes, professional, moving with a coordinated looseness civilians do not have. Reads as a group only to someone looking for a group. Not uniformed and not obviously armed.

COLE.name: Cole Porter
COLE.block:
Human, twenty-two years of physical work in the shoulders and hands. Heavy municipal work coat over practical layers in dull ochre and grey-green, tool belt, pouches, fingerless gloves, capped. A tradesman, never an adventurer.
>>> THE CANONICAL HAS THE LENS ON THE WRONG EYE. <<<
THE DIAGNOSTIC LENS GOES OVER HIS **LEFT** EYE — his own left, which is on the RIGHT side of the frame in a picture facing the viewer. The attached reference shows it over his right eye and that is an error awaiting a revision pass. MIRROR IT. Take everything else about the rig from the reference and put it on the other side of his face. His right eye is bare and human.
The rig itself: a scuffed, repaired municipal head rig — a strap around the skull, a short arm from the ear, a wide flat optic seated over the socket. Issued equipment worn daily for two decades. Not military, not elegant, nothing implanted.
WHEN THE LENS IS ACTIVE IT GLOWS AMBER-GOLD and throws a warm cast on that side of his face only. Note the deliberate split: the LENS runs warm, and the GRID OVERLAY it draws on the world runs electric blue. The tool is warm and the god's data is cold, and they must never be given the same colour.
THE PAPER NOTEBOOK is the plot object of the volume and appears in five plates: small, paper, worn soft at the corners, swollen with use, carried in the CHEST POCKET with a PENCIL. The reference does not show it clearly; wherever the notebook matters, draw it plainly and do not let a pouch or a radio stand in for it.
COLE.notes: Grid contractor, twenty-two years. Narrator of Prologue II. The lens is over the LEFT eye; the notebook is the plot object and appears in five plates.

THE_CARTOGRAPHER.name: The Man With The Book
THE_CARTOGRAPHER.block: HE MUST NOT BE MEMORABLE, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE DIRECTION. Cole can swear there was nothing unusual about him and afterward cannot say whether he was tall or short, old or young, or what his face looked like. Draw him accordingly: average height, average build, plain coat in a colour that is not a colour, a face with NO strong feature — no scar, no jaw, no distinctive nose, no memorable eyes, no augmentation, no expression worth naming. Keep him slightly turned, slightly soft, or slightly shadowed so the face never fully resolves, but do NOT hide it behind a mask, a hood or a blur effect — an obscured face is memorable and that is the opposite of what this is. He should read as somebody you have already forgotten while you are still looking at him. HE CARRIES A SMALL PAPER BOOK, worn soft at the corners and thick with use, and a PENCIL STUB. The book is the one thing about him anybody remembers, so the book is always clearly visible.
THE_CARTOGRAPHER.notes: Takes names in a paper book in the lost block. Deliberately has NO canonical reference: a locked face would destroy the character. p2 spreads 7 and 8.

SISTER_SILENCE.name: Sister Silence
SISTER_SILENCE.block:
Valari. Blue skin, long pointed ears, very long dark hair falling well past the waist. Follow the attached canonical exactly for face, colouring and vestments.
HER EYES ARE COVERED AND ARE NEVER VISIBLE. A fitted worked-GOLD CAP sits over the crown of her head and carries a solid gold band straight across the eyes. It is goldsmithing, not cloth — not a blindfold, not a bandage, not a visor with a lens, and nothing shows through it. Do not lift it, do not make it translucent, and do not draw eyes behind it.
VESTMENTS: heavy floor-length charcoal-black robes under a broad GOLD mantle across the shoulders, a gold orphrey band running the full centre front, a gold plaque belt, wide sleeves with gold facings, gold-trimmed hem, gold shoes. A cross-form emblem at the chest and repeated on the cap. She reads unmistakably as CLERGY. Rich, formal, immaculate.
IN SCENE SHE IS SMALL — shorter and slighter than the people around her. The canonical is a full-figure devotional sheet with nothing to measure her against, so take the geometry from it but never draw her as towering or imposing.
Her circuits are the FAINTEST SILVER, barely lit, like frost on glass — visible only as fine tracery at the hands and jaw. This is the one Valari whose circuits are silver instead of the usual blue-to-magenta-violet drift, and the exception is deliberate.
THE HORROR IS THE KINDNESS, AND WITH THE EYES COVERED IT ALL HAS TO LAND IN THE MOUTH AND THE TILT OF THE HEAD. Genuine, warm, unfaked care — the real thing, from somebody who believes completely that she is helping. Never sinister, never cold, never a strange smile. A viewer given only her face should think they are looking at a healer who loves her work.
SISTER_SILENCE.notes: One of the ten Oath Lords; her canonical came from references/OATH_LORDS. Takes memories. The Sandmen are hers. p2 spread 11.

GREY_CLIMB_WORN.value: Forty-seven days of climbing. The greatcoat is torn to tatters at hem and cuffs, scorched dark along one side, the red lining showing through the rips. Steel plating on face and hands is scorched, scuffed and heat-discoloured. The copper and brass mechanisms of the LEFT forearm are exposed and intermittently sparking. The suit beneath is filthy and torn. THE POCKET WATCH IS PRESENT on its chain, undamaged and clean - it is the one cared-for thing on him.
GREY_CLIMB_WORN.notes: Forty-seven days of climbing: plating scorched, coat torn to tatters, left-arm mechanisms sparking. Pocket watch present on its chain. p1 spreads 1-11.

GREY_POST_OATH.value: After the Glitch Engine. The greatcoat has been repaired but not restored - tears closed with visible seams and mismatched cloth, and it hangs differently than it did. The plating is still scorched; that damage is permanent now. THE POCKET WATCH IS GONE - no watch, no chain, nothing at the waistcoat where it hung. TWO FINGERS of one hand sit at a slightly wrong angle from the others, permanently. This is the state EVERY future appearance of Grey anywhere in the series must match.
GREY_POST_OATH.notes: After the Glitch Engine. Coat repaired but changed; pocket watch GONE; two fingers sit differently from the others. Everything from p1 spread 11 onward must match this, and so must every future appearance of Grey anywhere in the series.

PIXELS_GRID.notes: Pale blue grid pattern on the visor — what he shows when he wants to show nothing. t1 spreads 1-2.

PIXELS_BLANK.notes: No colour, no pattern, just dark glass in a pale frame — what he shows when the grid would be information. t1 spreads 3-4.

NYXARA_SUPPRESSED.value: Her circuits are DIM and LOW — soft blue drifting toward dusty magenta-violet, unsaturated, suppressed by the city field and by her own effort. They are present and readable but they do not light anything around them and they never glow. This is her condition in every Prologue III plate.
NYXARA_SUPPRESSED.notes: Circuits dim and low — the city field plus her own effort. Her default in every p3 plate.

TAL_VOSS_HIDDEN.value: His circuits are HIDDEN, down to almost nothing — not dimmed like Nyx'ara's, but deliberately shut down beneath the demon mask. At most a faint trace where the mask meets the neck. This is his condition in every Prologue III plate.
TAL_VOSS_HIDDEN.notes: Circuits hidden to almost nothing beneath the demon mask. Deliberate, not suppression. His default in every p3 plate.

PEAK_CHAMBER.name: the chamber at the peak of the Tower
PEAK_CHAMBER.block: Interior at the top of the Tower. Faceted crystal in pale gold, cold white and slate blue - cut and angular, never organic. Spires and outcrops rise from the floor at intervals, large enough for a figure to brace against or hook an arm over. The floor is FULLY TRANSPARENT with Haven City far below through it: street grid, the Valari Quarter as a soft blue patch, the wasteland beyond. The walls open onto a horizon at the same level as that floor-city - a spatial contradiction that is CORRECT and must be preserved; scale here is deliberately unresolvable, vast and impossibly small at once. Light falls from the peak overhead.
PEAK_CHAMBER.notes: Crystalline. Or vast. Or impossibly small — contradictory truths hold here the way they do in dreams or mathematics. Transparent floor with Haven City far below. p1 spreads 1-4, 8-11.

HAVEN_CITY_AERIAL.name: Haven City from above
HAVEN_CITY_AERIAL.block: Haven City from very high above. A walled quadrilateral city on a rust-red wasteland plain, its street grid orthogonal and dense like a circuit board soldered onto the earth. Four zones stay separable: the VALARI QUARTER glowing soft blue at one side; the INDUSTRIAL BLOCKS dark and square; the civic core; and the WASTELAND outside the wall, rust-coloured to the horizon. The TOWER rises through the centre like a needle - gold, faceted, stepped back in setbacks, one vertical seam of light up its full height. At this distance the Valari Quarter reads as a single blue mass; the blue / magenta-violet drift of individual circuits is only visible close up.
HAVEN_CITY_AERIAL.notes: Street grid like a circuit board soldered onto the earth. Valari Quarter glowing faint blue, industrial blocks dark and square, the Wasteland out to the horizon, the Tower through the middle like a needle. p1 spreads 1 and 12.

MARKET_DISTRICT.name: the Market District
MARKET_DISTRICT.block: Street level. Vendor stalls in rows at identical intervals under orange awnings, pale cream and sand stone, navy structural linework, goods stacked with unsettling regularity. Crowd-flow corridors are marked into the paving itself as inlaid lines and circular medallions. Smooth, clean, airless efficiency - it looks like abundance and functions like a clock. Nothing is crooked, handmade, cluttered or improvised. The discomfort comes from the REGULARITY, never from decay: this is not a slum and not a ruin.
MARKET_DISTRICT.notes: Smooth, airless efficiency — it looks like abundance and functions like a clock. Vendor rows, crowd-flow corridors measured to fractions. p1 spreads 5-7.

WASTELAND.name: the Wasteland outside Haven City's walls
WASTELAND.block: Outside Haven City's walls. Oxidised structure half-buried in rust-coloured ground: collapsed infrastructure, corroded spans, drum forms, the bones of machinery that was never repaired. Flat, long sightlines, nothing moving, nothing alive. Haven City's WALL runs across the middle distance and the TOWER rises behind it and out of the top of frame, gold and faceted with its vertical light seam. This is where the world ended.
WASTELAND.notes: Rust and silence where the world ended and was never repaired. The Tower going up out of frame. p1 spread 13, and the p1 opener.

COURIERS_EXCHANGE.name: the Courier's Exchange
COURIERS_EXCHANGE.block: Interior. A working dispatch room: long sorting tables with worn tops, pigeonhole racks along one wall, hanging task boards, stacked pouches and sealed packets, a claim counter at the back. Municipal, utilitarian, built for throughput. A TALL WINDOW on one side throws hard directional light across the nearest table in a sharp-edged shape - that light is the reason the room exists, and its direction and hardness must not change.
COURIERS_EXCHANGE.notes: Where dispatch work is handed out. Window light on a working table. t1 spread 1.

RECLAMATION_ALLEY.name: the alley behind the water reclamation building
RECLAMATION_ALLEY.block: Night, rain. A narrow alley behind the water reclamation building with both walls in frame. Bulk pipework, condensate lines, valve housings, vent stacks and grated drains on both sides; standing water, runoff pouring from outlets, rain visibly falling in the air. Two blocks north the alley opens onto a cross street where a BONE PATROL CHECKPOINT is running: its cold white light turns the falling rain SILVER at that end of frame. Dark alley, lit far end - the distance between them is the composition.
RECLAMATION_ALLEY.notes: Narrow, wet, rain finding the gaps. Bone Patrol checkpoint lights turning the rain silver two blocks north. t1 opener and spread 2.

PATROL_STATION.name: Third Patrol Station, Sector Four
PATROL_STATION.block: Interior. The vehicle and processing bay of Third Patrol Station: structural ribs, high ceiling, poured floor with painted lane and chevron markings, equipment lockers and rack frames with small red indicators, a processing counter along one side. A WIDE EXIT DOORWAY at the far end with two flanking piers - those two positions are where officers stand and must not move. NOTE: this canonical is lit dark. When a figure has to cross the bay, ask for one additional working overhead fixture near the middle so they do not become a silhouette in a black room.
PATROL_STATION.notes: The patrol bay and its exit. t1 spread 3.

RESIDENTIAL_BLOCK_14.name: Residential Block 14, third floor
RESIDENTIAL_BLOCK_14.block: Interior, night. A narrow stairwell arriving at a third-floor landing, and the hallway running off it past apartment doors. Warm and dim: a single caged fixture, ochre and amber light, deep shadow. Heavy panelled doors with mechanical latches and SECURITY CHAINS. A wall-mounted RADIATOR with dried protein strips laid across it to cure. Scuffed panelling, low ceiling, worn floor. A window on the stair landing shows the lit city at night. Cramped, tired, lived-in and cared for.
RESIDENTIAL_BLOCK_14.notes: Narrow stairwell, third-floor hallway, a radiator with dried protein strips on it. t1 spread 4.

WELLNESS_CENTER.name: the Wellness and Optimization Center
WELLNESS_CENTER.block: Dusk. A low, wide, calm institutional frontage in pale cream limestone with tall glazed bays, approached across a clean forecourt with planting and ground lanterns. Behind the glass: a tall daylit ATRIUM with a curved ceiling and skylights, a still REFLECTING POOL set into the floor, and the INTAKE DESK at the far side with terminal stations behind it. A recessed SERVICE OPENING on the right of the atrium leads into a narrow, cooler, strip-lit MAINTENANCE CORRIDOR - easy to overlook, and the route to the service lane. IT IS DESIGNED TO LOOK LIKE MEDICINE and must be genuinely reassuring: the horror is that it is beautiful. Never sinister, never clinical-cold.
WELLNESS_CENTER.notes: Calm institutional facade, atrium with a reflecting pool, intake desk. Designed to look like medicine. t2 opener and spreads 1-4.

SERVICE_LANE.name: the service lane behind the Wellness Center
SERVICE_LANE.block: Night. The rear elevation of the Wellness Center - the same pale cream limestone and flat roofline as its front, but blank and windowless, with extract ducting, plant housings, conduit, junction boxes, loading bays and waste bins bolted onto good stone. A UTILITY DOOR in the near wall up a short step, a lamp above it, cool corridor light spilling out. The lane runs away into darkness and meets the eastern residential district at the far end: blocky angular Haven City blocks with warm, ordinary, occupied windows. Dark lane, somewhere to go lit at the end.
SERVICE_LANE.notes: Reached through a utility door off the maintenance corridor; connects to the eastern residential district. t2 spread 4.

THE_PRISM.name: The Prism
THE_PRISM.block:
Interior. Rainbow's bar, and it is NOT a small room — it is a big, deep, busy room and every plate set here must show enough of it to feel that. It has FOUR DISTINCT ZONES, and each plate is assigned one:
  ZONE 1 — THE BAR. A long bar down one side with a row of stools. Behind it a back bar of bottles lit warm AMBER, with a small screen mounted above. This zone is warm. "THE WALL" means the far end of the bar away from the front door, and Sable's seat is the THIRD STOOL counting from that end, every time.
  ZONE 2 — THE FLOOR. Open standing room between the bar and the booths, with the FRONT DOOR at one end and a separate SIDE ENTRANCE off it. Tall enough and wide enough that a large chassis can cross it. Lit MAGENTA and VIOLET from above. This is the loudest zone.
  ZONE 3 — THE BOOTHS. Corner booths with red banquettes along the far wall, and one CORNER TABLE set apart from the rest. Lit low and DEEP BLUE, with the room's neon falling off before it reaches here — the quiet zone in a loud room.
  ZONE 4 — THE BACK ROOM. Up ONE STEP through a wide opening: a deeper space of loose tables where a group can sit apart, with heavy columns, a low ceiling and cooler TEAL and GREEN light. Signal takes a table here. It must be visibly a different room from the bar, not more of the same one.
Deep navy structure throughout ties the four zones together. The COLOUR CHANGES BY ZONE and that is deliberate: it is what lets six plates in one location look like six different pictures.
THE_PRISM.notes: Rainbow's bar at the end of the approach road to the Tower gate. Four zones — bar, floor, booths, back room up a step — because p3 sets six plates here and one narrow room could only ever produce one shot. p3 spreads 1-6, and p4 spreads 8-10.

TOWER_PLAZA.name: the Tower ground plaza
TOWER_PLAZA.block: The public square at the foot of the Tower. Mirror-polished pale stone floor; a ring of pale glass towers around it; the TOWER rising gold and faceted from the far side with its arched gate of receding arches at the base. The REGISTRATION WALL stands across the front of the plaza facing the crowd - a broad, flat, monumental pale surface people walk up to and set a palm against. SCREENS on every surrounding building face at several sizes and heights, carrying an abstract feed and NEVER readable text. One SMALL CRACKED DISPLAY above a water station at the plaza edge. Chain-post perimeter; the eastern streets enter at one side. Holds three hundred on a quiet week.
TOWER_PLAZA.notes: Holds three hundred on a quiet week. The registration wall at the front. Screens on every building face carrying the registration feed. p3 spreads 7-18.

TOWER_GATE.name: the Tower gate
TOWER_GATE.block: The Tower's gate. Enormous: geometric lines layered back in receding arches the way a cathedral is layered, gold light filling the opening, a vertical seam of white light rising out of the arch, faceted gold-and-navy mass around it, mirror-polished approach floor. THE GATE SIMPLY STANDS OPEN. It has no doors, no leaves, no hinges, no mechanism, nothing that could ever be shut. It has always been open and it lets you decide. When light 'closes behind' someone passing through, that is an optical effect of depth and glare, never a door.
TOWER_GATE.notes: Enormous and gold-lit, geometric lines layered back in receding arches the way a cathedral is layered — except it simply stands open and lets you decide. Always open. Visible from The Prism's door on clear mornings. p3 spread 18 and the opener.

APPROACH_ROAD.name: the approach road
APPROACH_ROAD.block: The broad street running from the Tower gate - visible small and gold at one end - down past THE PRISM, the building with the triangular faceted window over its entrance. Across the street from The Prism is a TRANSIT HUB, and mounted on a bracket above it is a SURVEILLANCE NODE: a compact armoured housing on a curved bracket with a cable, high enough that a failure drops it about eight feet to hang from that cable. Blocky angular Haven City architecture both sides, warm ochre morning light low along the street. The node is intact and powered unless a plate says otherwise.
APPROACH_ROAD.notes: Runs from the Tower gate down past The Prism. Transit hub across the street with a surveillance node above it. p3 spreads 19-20.

BLOCK_44_SURFACE.name: Block 44, street level
BLOCK_44_SURFACE.block: An ordinary Haven City residential street during a GLITCH STUTTER. Corridor and street lighting at HALF POWER, uneven, some fixtures out entirely. Doors along the block WEDGED OPEN with whatever came to hand and windows CRACKED open — a habit the block has developed, done without being told, the way shutters get closed before a storm. Older construction than the Tower district: heavy blockwork, exposed conduit runs, service hatches. At one end, the WATER RECLAMATION BUILDING with an ACCESS SHAFT behind it. Nothing is dramatic and nothing is ruined; this is a working neighbourhood having a bad evening.

SUB_LEVEL_GALLERY.name: Block 44 sub-level service gallery
SUB_LEVEL_GALLERY.block: A long, low SERVICE GALLERY under Block 44. Pipe and conduit run along BOTH walls in tagged, numbered municipal runs. Standing water on the floor, two inches and rising, holding reflections. The far end of the gallery is BLACK — the only light is what Cole brings with him, a shoulder lamp throwing a long cone that ends in nothing. At the NORTH wall, a heavy unmarked FEEDER PIPE enters the gallery through what the map calls solid foundation, and four meters east of it the painted-over outline of a MAINTENANCE DOOR, sealed so long its hinges are under sixty years of paint. Pre-Seraph construction: older, heavier and cruder than anything on the surface.

THE_LOST_BLOCK.name: The block that fell off the map
THE_LOST_BLOCK.block: An entire SUB-LEVEL STREET, underground and low-ceilinged, that the city has no record of. Strings of small WHITE LAMPS run its length, wired clean and spliced by somebody who knew what they were doing. LAUNDRY on lines between the support columns. A GARDEN of pale vegetables under GROW LAMPS, planted in beds built out of lifted paving stones. A CISTERN with a valve rig on it that is better work than most municipal jobs. Twenty or thirty small DWELLINGS with CURTAINS for doors. A child's CHALK DRAWING loops across the paving. THIS PLACE IS NOT A SLUM, A HIDEOUT OR A RUIN. It is maintained, lit, planted and lived in, and it is warmer and more human than anything on the surface. Somebody is always cooking. Draw it as a home.

WHITE_ROOM.name: The white room
WHITE_ROOM.block: WHITE TILE walls, a WHITE CEILING, and light arriving from EVERY DIRECTION AT ONCE so that the room contains NO SHADOWS ANYWHERE. That is the defining fact and it must be absolute: no cast shadow under the table, none under a chin, none behind a figure, no falloff into any corner. Nothing in the room reads as three-dimensional in the normal way, because shadow is what normally does that. A single TABLE at the centre, and the table is COMFORTABLE — padded, clean, considerate, the sort of surface built for somebody's ease. That detail is the worst thing in the room and it must be legible. No restraints, no instruments, no medical clutter, no gore, no menace in the props. This room is frightening BECAUSE it is gentle.
WHITE_ROOM.notes: p2 spread 11. The one plate in the volume with no palette mode.
